what_differs_fadd_verbatim: **fadd.ps**: with one-number vectors no data line switches in steady state, for any value. The only modelled differences are the bubbles between instructions (2 x popcount of the sum per bubble: 8.0 has 2 one-bits, 10.0 has 3) and the leakage of the held state. They nearly cancel: 5s cost about 9 fJ more per instruction, about 1e-4 of the instruction's modelled energy.

ledger.words_verbatim: In fadd.ps no data line switches in steady state. The only modelled differences are the bubbles between instructions, set by the popcount of the sum, and the held state's leakage. They nearly cancel.

against_lab.definition_verbatim: Full model = every modelled on-die line above the zeros anchor, including the register-file lines. Measured = the lab's board power above its zeros anchor and its minion-rail share, divided by the measured op rate.

caveat_verbatim: The fadd.ps one-number row compares about 0.07 pJ modelled with a measured +0.44 / +0.40 pJ. On one card that step is inside the run-to-run spread, but the lab's three cards all read +0.40 to +0.49 pJ, and on one of them the step is about five standard errors. So a constant nonzero operand does cost more than zeros, about 6-7x what october-forecast-model gives: the model misses a value-dependent static term.
